findings.passage: Our leading read on Daniela Amodei's personality type is Enneagram Type 1, the Reformer, at medium confidence.
findings.problem: After the repair, the record states plainly that nothing separates One from Two. Type_hypothesis.discriminator says "No clean discriminator yet separates One from Two," C167 says no observation in the record discriminates, and the body says "A Two in her job who has learned that candor helps could produce the same record." The standard says to use insufficient_evidence "when no defensible discriminator exists." The open-case route does not apply: she has run Anthropic publicly since 2021 and has 15+ long-form first-person sources, so this is a deep record whose type is hard, which the standard says "remains insufficient_evidence with research tasks." "Medium confidence" in the type answer, type FAQ and Dario FAQ claims more than an undiscriminated lean supports, which is why enneagram-01's "confidence is lowered to match" is unmet. The owner note in the research file asks for exactly this hold if Type 1 cannot clear the release bar. The writing and sourcing are not the problem: the repair made the article honest. The problem is that an honest standard profile cannot yet answer its own title question.
findings.acceptance_test: The evidence record gains at least one opened, attributed observation from a setting where a relational motive could surface: named colleague testimony on what she does when someone misses a standard or cuts a corner, or her own non-promotional account of a choice where warmth and a standard collided. It must be one that a Two-motivated executive in her role would be unlikely to produce. The type answer, type FAQ and "Why not Type 2?" then argue One over Two from it, the Six lean is re-tested, and the stated confidence matches the argument. Until then the run stays insufficient_evidence; certainty is not raised by argument alone. If the new evidence favors Two, the leading type changes and the run needs --refresh --expanded-review.

findings.passage: "We were running towards something versus running away from something," she told Stanford GSB.
findings.problem: Her spoken words in the GSB transcript (S01) are "I think we're running towards something, versus running away from something." The printed "We were" comes from GSB's editorial pull-quote. The meaning is unchanged, but "she told" attributes the pull-quote wording to her speech.
findings.acceptance_test: The quote uses the transcript wording ("we're running towards something, versus running away from something"), or the sentence attributes the past-tense rendering to Stanford GSB's write-up.

findings.passage: Anthropic largely won in district court on August 27, 2026, lost before a split appeals panel on September 25, and was seeking rehearing as of the October filing.
findings.problem: The S-1 describes two separate challenges. In N.D. Cal., over the Department's directive, the Section 3252 designation and the Presidential directive, Anthropic won summary judgment on 2026-08-27. In the D.C. Circuit, on a petition for review of the separate Section 4713 designation, a 2-1 panel ruled against it on 2026-09-25, and en banc rehearing was sought. As written, the appeals loss reads as reversing the district-court win.
findings.acceptance_test: The sentence distinguishes the two tracks, e.g. "Anthropic largely won in district court on August 27, 2026; in a separate challenge to a second designation, a split D.C. Circuit panel ruled against it on September 25, and it was seeking rehearing as of the October filing." C145 stays unresolved with its trigger.

findings.passage: Capitol Hill didn't last: "It just was slow and bureaucratic," she said at Stanford in 2024.
findings.problem: In the same sentence (S04) she gives a second reason: "I missed the campaign days of getting to build something together with a small group of, you know, motivated people." The relational half bears on the 1-vs-2 question the article is weighing. It is the same trim pattern the jury flagged elsewhere, though here it does not tilt toward One.
findings.acceptance_test: The passage adds or fairly paraphrases her second reason (building something with a small, motivated group). The protected inference about procedure stays, scoped to the first reason.

findings.passage: She wants candidates who can say "I changed my mind because I actually realized, you know, I wasn't right about this."
findings.problem: In Vanta (S33 13:48) the culture interview looks for either "I felt this was the correct thing and maybe it wasn't popular, but like I really stood by this" or "I changed my mind..." The article quotes only the second half, as evidence she is pragmatic about values. The omitted half is One-relevant.
findings.acceptance_test: The sentence gives both halves (standing by an unpopular correct position, or changing one's mind), and the "pragmatic about values" point is weighed against the first half.

research_tasks: Find named, on-record testimony about how she responds when someone misses a standard or cuts a corner. Sources: Anthropic's chief people officer (referenced at S29 05:31), on-record Stripe-era colleagues (the mentor/Claire Hughes Johnson link is unverified), and OpenAI-era colleagues. This is the observation that would separate One from Two (a One holds the line on the work; a Two moves toward the person) and would sharpen One vs Six. It can move the read either way.

Find a non-promotional first-person account where warmth and a standard collided and she says which she chose and why. Look in long-form interviews outside recruiting and launch settings, The Times (2024-06-24, S26, unretrieved) and TIME May 2024, especially on personal decisions (leaving Stripe, the 2020 OpenAI exit) where a relational motive could surface.

Identify from video who says "I credit Daniela with keeping the bar high" (S38 00:34:29) and whom "you're the reason the culture scaled" addresses (00:34:40). It is the only third-party datum on the One side, and a named speaker would raise its weight.

Seek on-record accounts (Daniela, Brockman, Altman or Radford) of the language-project standoff, the coup accusation and the March 2020 peer reviews (S13, S39, S12). Until then they stay disputed and corroborative only.
After the IPO, read Anthropic's first proxy and governance disclosures for how the board reviews its president and chair (C51) and any revenue-over-principle trade-off she explains (C49, C102).
Track the D.C. Circuit en banc petition on the Section 4713 designation and any appeal of the N.D. Cal. judgment (C145).
